title: "Tutorial 8 — Self-check answers"
sidebar: mfml
---

1. Likelihood has $\log\sum_j$ mixture terms, so gradients couple components.  
2. $\gamma_{ij}=\dfrac{\alpha_j\mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_j,\Sigma_j)}{\sum_k\alpha_k\mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_k,\Sigma_k)}$ at current $\theta$.  
3. $\alpha_j=N_j/n$, $\mu_j=N_j^{-1}\sum_i\gamma_{ij}x_i$, $\Sigma_j=N_j^{-1}\sum_i\gamma_{ij}(x_i-\mu_j)(x_i-\mu_j)^\top$.  
4. $N_j=\sum_i\gamma_{ij}$ (soft count for component $j$).  
5. Spherical equal covariances $\sigma^2 I$ with $\sigma\to 0$ harden responsibilities into nearest-mean assignments; mean updates become K-means.
